replacement.title: Harborline Thrive Retention and Elementor Migration
replacement.definition: Retain Thrive where required to preserve existing page styling while using Elementor for new pages and postponing full Thrive removal or migration until the replacement site is ready.

patches.decision_note: The page-builder retention and migration strategy can evolve independently from remediation of vulnerable plugins and should not remain embedded in the plugin-security Requirement.
Disabling Thrive Apprentice is plugin-security remediation, but postponing removal of the Thrive page builder belongs to the separate page-builder retention and migration Requirement.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Current status: the site layout has been fully recovered, Wordfence has been configured for security, malware has been removed from around 34 outdated plugins, and all fake admins have been removed.

Follow-up work remains. Although the pages appear fine, I cannot verify whether all the private pages work correctly. Please test every contact form and change your admin password. For the search-engine cleanup, I still need Search Console access for Stonefield as well.

**Overall report**
There are signs of earlier, smaller-scale attacks dating back to 2022. The majority of the 14000 posts were injected on October 14th, and all of the website's pages were deleted on December 20th.

execution.observed_behavior: Investigation established that attackers injected the majority of approximately 14,000 Stonefield posts.

patches.decision_note: This is the first concrete failure evidence for Stonefield's injected-content cleanup and is distinct from legitimate-page recovery and malicious-code removal.
